symbols.name: tc
symbols.def: \(\overline D\) contains \(i\to j\) exactly when \(D\) has a directed path from \(i\) to \(j\)

symbols.name: Lambda
symbols.def: \(\Lambda^{(k)}=\Lambda^{(0)}+e_k\delta_k^{\mathsf T}\) for \(k\in V\), with \(\Lambda^{(0)}\) at context \(0\)

symbols.name: Sk
symbols.type: indexed family of positive diagonal matrices

symbols.name: Qexc
symbols.role: explicit exceptional-polynomial lists for the terminal, branch, square, and fork results

symbols.name: Mgen
symbols.role: relative Zariski-open subset of the semialgebraic ambient domain

symbols.name: E
symbols.role: true parameter points admitting a legal covariance twin

symbols.name: Mon
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak M_q=\{\Pi C:\Pi\text{ is a permutation matrix and }C\text{ is nonsingular diagonal}\}\)

symbols.name: Ralign
symbols.role: explicit population input recovered before graph compatibility is evaluated

symbols.name: HR
symbols.role: actual-row coordinates obtained from the aligned population factor updates

symbols.name: GHdata
symbols.role: DAGs compatible with the aligned population factorization datum

symbols.name: GCdata
symbols.role: DAGs with the factor-recovered closure that are compatible with the observed covariance tuple

symbols.name: Lmat
symbols.role: candidate baseline loading matrix on a branch

symbols.name: vprime
symbols.role: candidate baseline error variances on a branch

symbols.name: TRF
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{TRF}(D)\) holds when, for every nonsink \(k\), the parent set \(\operatorname{pa}_{D}(k)\) is an antichain under reachability in \(D\); equivalently, no transitive edge enters a nonsink

symbols.name: T
symbols.role: free true intervention variance in the worked fork family

symbols.name: Wfork
symbols.type: one-parameter pair of soft-intervention parameter points

symbols.name: Enc
symbols.role: compiler input and sparse branch-polynomial encoding

novel.justification: This is the paper's deliberate square-or-overcomplete scope restriction, not a restriction attributed to the standard LCD regime. It includes square systems and measurement settings with more latent mechanisms than observed coordinates, while isolating the noninjective frontier \(p<q\).

assumptions.condition: The labels in \(V\) form a topological order of \(G\).
\(\Lambda^{(0)}_{ij}\ne0\) if and only if \(j\to i\) is an edge of \(G\).
No two columns of \(F\) are collinear.

standard.name: Single-node soft intervention changing every incoming edge

novel.justification: This retained-edge soft-intervention condition describes perturbations that modify rather than delete active regulatory inputs; any continuously distributed perturbation away from the finitely many deletion values satisfies it almost surely.

assumptions.condition: The coordinates of \(\varepsilon^{(k)}\) are mutually independent in every context \(k\in K\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M_{p,q}(G)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{p,q}(G)=\{(F,\Lambda^{(0)},\delta,v,t)\in\mathbb R^{pq+2q^2+2q}:2\le p\le q,\operatorname{rank}(F)=p,\ F\text{ has nonzero pairwise-noncollinear columns},\Lambda^{(0)}_{ij}\ne0\Longleftrightarrow j\to i\text{ is an edge of }G,\operatorname{supp}(\delta_k)=\operatorname{pa}_G(k),\Lambda^{(0)}_{kj}+\delta_{kj}\ne0,\ v_i>0,\ t_i>0\}\). This positive-support semialgebraic ambient domain includes the variance-neutral hyperplanes \(t_i=v_i\). All equalities, strict inequalities, closures, relative interiors, and chambers below use the Euclidean relative topology of this ambient set or of a stated semialgebraic subset.

definitions.name: Finite theorem-specific exceptional-polynomial families
definitions.construction: For a fixed graph pair, \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{term}}\) consists of the nonzero terminal-linkage minors and augmented affine-support minors used by the terminal certificate. The family \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{branch}}\) consists of the nonzero rank minors, factor-line discriminants, denominator-cleared chart denominators, support residuals, and the variance-activity factor \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)\) used by the covariance branches. The family \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{square}}\) contains the branch factors and adds the nonzero whitening pivots and ancestor-order inner products used by square recovery. For the fork pair, \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{fork}}\) contains the specialized branch factors and adds every nonzero \(3\times3\) minor of \(B_{\ell}\), \(\det[\ell_1,\ell_2]\), \(\det[\ell_3,\ell_4]\), \(\det[g,\ell_3]\), \(\det[g,\ell_4]\), and every nonzero maximal minor of the Jacobian of each denominator-cleared two-scalar branch system with respect to its candidate variables. Each list is finite and is formed after deleting the polynomials that vanish identically for the fixed graph pair. Thus variance neutrality is excluded only from the covariance theorem loci, not from \(\mathcal M_{p,q}(G)\) or \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{term}}\).

definitions.name: Theorem-specific generic loci
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{s,p,q}(G,G')=\{\theta\in\mathcal M_{p,q}(G):\prod_{f\in\mathcal Q_s(p,G,G')}f(\theta)\ne0\}\) for \(s\in\{\mathrm{term},\mathrm{branch},\mathrm{square},\mathrm{fork}\}\), equipped with the relative Zariski topology inherited from the semialgebraic ambient domain. The factor \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)\) belongs only to the branch, square, and fork families, so terminal compatibility is not restricted by variance activity.

definitions.name: Aligned population factorization input \(\mathcal R\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal R=[\{A^{(k)}\}_{k\in K},\{\mathcal L(\varepsilon^{(k)})\}_{k\in K}]_{\mathfrak M_q}\), where columns and independent non-Gaussian source laws are aligned across contexts. For \(M\in\mathfrak M_q\), the equivalence action is \(A^{(k)}\mapsto A^{(k)}M\) and \(\mathcal L(\varepsilon^{(k)})\mapsto\mathcal L(M^{-1}\varepsilon^{(k)})\) simultaneously for every \(k\in K\). This factorization datum is an explicit population input; its recovery from raw laws is not assumed inside the graph-compatibility map.

definitions.name: Factor-recovered actual-row support and closure
definitions.construction: Choose any representative of \(\mathcal R\). For each aligned target \(k\), solve the rank-one update \(A^{(k)}=A^{(0)}+a_kh_{\mathcal R,k}^{\mathsf T}\) with \(h_{\mathcal R,kk}=0\), and form \(H_{\mathcal R}\) from these rows. Define \(\mathcal C(\mathcal R)\) by \(i\to k\in\mathcal C(\mathcal R)\Longleftrightarrow(H_{\mathcal R})_{ki}\ne0\).

definitions.name: Observable-input graph classes
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R)=\{D:D\text{ is a DAG on }V,\ \overline D=\mathcal C(\mathcal R),\text{ and there exist }\theta\in\mathcal M_{p,q}(D)\text{ and independent centered non-Gaussian }\varepsilon^{(k)}\text{ with covariance }S^{(k)}\text{ whose aligned factorization represents }\mathcal R\}\). Also \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{cov}}(\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K})=\{D:D\text{ is a DAG on }V,\ \overline D=\mathcal C(\mathcal R),\text{ and some }\theta\in\mathcal M_{p,q}(D)\text{ generates every }\Sigma^{(k)}\}\). Both sets are taken modulo the common relabeling induced by \(\mathfrak M_q\).

definitions.name: Terminal-copy graph \(G^{\mathrm{term}}\)
definitions.construction: Starting from \(G\), add a sink \(k^{\star}\) for each \(k\in V\); retain every baseline edge and add \(i\to k^{\star}\) with label \(\delta_{ki}\) for each \(i\in\operatorname{pa}_{G}(k)\).

definitions.name: Terminal-reuse-free graph condition
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{TRF}(G)\Longleftrightarrow[\operatorname{ch}_{G}(k)\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow\operatorname{pa}_{G}(k)\text{ is an antichain in }\overline G]\) for every \(k\in V\). Its forbidden configuration is a transitive edge \(u\to k\), a directed path of length at least two from \(u\) to \(k\), and an outgoing edge \(k\to w\).

definitions.name: Columnwise affine compatibility block
definitions.construction: For every \(j\in V\), set \(C_j=\operatorname{ch}_{G'}(j)\), \(R_j=\operatorname{de}_{G'}(j)\setminus C_j\), \(M_j=H[R_j,C_j]\), \(b_j=H[R_j,j]\), \(\mathcal A_j=\{x_j\in\mathbb R^{|C_j|}:M_jx_j=b_j\}\), and \(d_{ji}(x_j)=H[i,j]-H[i,C_j]x_j\) for \(i\in C_j\).

definitions.name: Published observational-path class \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{obs}}(G)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{obs}}(G)=\{G':\overline{G'}=\overline G,\ \operatorname{rank}P[R_j,C_j]=\operatorname{rank}P[R_j,C_j\cup\{j\}]\text{ for every }j\in V\text{ and every }\theta\in\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{term},p,q}(G,G')\}\).

definitions.name: Corrected actual-row class \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)=\{G':\overline{G'}=\overline G,\text{ for every }\theta\in\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{term},p,q}(G,G')\text{ there exists }U=I_q-\Lambda'^{(0)}\text{ with exact support }G'\text{ such that }h_k^{\mathsf T}U\text{ has exact support }\operatorname{pa}_{G'}(k)\text{ and every candidate edge remains nonzero after its change for all }k\in V\}\).

definitions.name: Positive-real covariance twin set \(\mathcal E_p(G,G')\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E_p(G,G')=\{\theta\in\mathcal M_{p,q}(G):\exists\theta'\in\mathcal M_{p,q}(G')\text{ with }\Sigma_{\theta'}^{(k)}=\Sigma_{\theta}^{(k)}\text{ for every }k\in K\}\). Candidate baseline and intervention variances are positive but may satisfy \(t'_k=v'_k\); variance activity is imposed only on a true theorem-specific generic locus.

definitions.name: Generic positive-real covariance class \(\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)=\{G':\overline{G'}=\overline G,\ C\setminus\operatorname{cl}_{C}(\mathcal E_p(G,G')\cap C)\text{ has empty }\operatorname{relint}_{C}\text{ for every full-dimensional connected semialgebraic chamber }C\text{ of }\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{branch},p,q}(G,G')\}\), where the chambers fix the signs of the nonzero structural coefficients, changes, and \(t_k-v_k\), and closure and relative interior are taken in \(C\). This is a generic chamberwise functional and makes no pointwise assertion on the variance-neutral hyperplanes of the ambient model.

definitions.name: Worked fork covariance collision \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{fork}}(T)\)
definitions.construction: For \(p=2\), \(q=4\), and \(T>0\), \(T\ne1\), set the true baseline loading and variances to \(A=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&2&7&4\\2&3&11&7\end{psmallmatrix}\) and \(v=(1,1,1,1)\); set \(\Lambda^{(0)}_{21}=\Lambda^{(0)}_{31}=\Lambda^{(0)}_{32}=\Lambda^{(0)}_{42}=1\), \(h_1=0\), \(h_2=(1,0,0,0)\), \(h_3=(3,1,0,0)\), \(h_4=(1,1,0,0)\), and \(t=(4,4,T,4)\), with \(F=A(I_4-\Lambda^{(0)})\). For the candidate set \(\Lambda'^{(0)}_{21}=4\), \(\Lambda'^{(0)}_{32}=\Lambda'^{(0)}_{42}=1\), \(F'=\begin{psmallmatrix}-7&-9&7&4\\-10&-15&11&7\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(v'=(1,1,1,1)\), \(h'_1=0\), \(h'_2=(1,0,0,0)\), \(h'_3=(32/11,8/11,0,0)\), \(h'_4=(-2,-1/2,0,0)\), and \(t'=(4,4,T+144/121,19/4)\). In both models define each change row by \(\delta_k^{\mathsf T}=h_k^{\mathsf T}(I_4-\Lambda^{(0)})\) and its primed analogue, and use independent centered non-Gaussian errors with the displayed variances.

definitions.name: Complete generic factor-line branch family \(\mathfrak B_p(G,G')\)
definitions.construction: For \(\theta\in\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{branch},p,q}(G,G')\), factor each \(D_k\) as \(D_k=\ell_km_k^{\mathsf T}+m_k\ell_k^{\mathsf T}\), choose one of its two real factor lines for each nonroot and its unique line for each root, and for that choice impose \(L\operatorname{diag}(v')L^{\mathsf T}=\Sigma^{(0)}\), \(Lz_k+\rho_k\ell_k=m_k\), \(z_k\) supported on \(\operatorname{an}_{G'}(k)\), \(t'_k=v'_k+2\rho_k-\sum_i z_{ki}^2/v'_i>0\), \(\delta_k'{}^{\mathsf T}=z_k^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{diag}(v')^{-1}U\), and every exact-support, retained-edge, and mixing-column inequation; \(\mathfrak B_p(G,G')\) is the resulting family of at most \(2^{q-r}\) systems. Candidate variance-neutral branches remain legal.

definitions.name: Eight explicit bivariate fork systems
definitions.construction:
For each of the eight loading-line choices, form \(B_{\ell}=[(\ell_{k1}^2,\ell_{k1}\ell_{k2},\ell_{k2}^2)^{\mathsf T}]_{k=1}^{4}\), solve \(v'=v'_0+sn\) with \(n\in\ker B_{\ell}\setminus\{0\}\), write \(m_2=\zeta\ell_1+ho_2\ell_2\), and set \(g=v'_1x\ell_1+v'_2\ell_2\). For \(k\in\{3,4\}\), impose \( eta_k=\det[m_k,\ell_k]/\det[g,\ell_k]\), \(m_k- eta_kg=ho_k\ell_k\), \(h'_2=(\zeta/v'_1,0,0,0)\), \(h'_k= eta_k(x,1,0,0)\), \(t'_2=v'_2+2ho_2-\zeta^2/v'_1\), and \(t'_k=v'_k+2ho_k- eta_k^2(v'_1x^2+v'_2)\). The system includes \(v'_i>0\), \(t'_i>0\), \(x
e0\), \(x+\zeta/v'_1
e0\), \(\zeta eta_3 eta_4\det[g,\ell_3]\det[g,\ell_4]
e0\), the stated mixing noncollinearities, and finite hyperplane avoidance for the remaining coefficients \(\Lambda'^{(0)}_{32}\) and \(\Lambda'^{(0)}_{42}\). Candidate equalities \(t'_i=v'_i\) are not excluded. Thus each legal branch is a rational sign system only in \(s\) and \(x\).

definitions.name: Graph and sparse-polynomial bit model
definitions.construction: Encode \(p\) and \(q\) in binary, encode \(G\) and \(G'\) by their \(q\times q\) adjacency bit matrices in the common topological order, and encode every denominator-cleared input branch polynomial sparsely by binary exponent vectors and signed binary integer coefficients. Let \(B=|\operatorname{Enc}(p,G,G')|_{\mathrm{bit}}\) be this pre-solution input length; certificate coefficient growth is part of the output complexity to be bounded.

definitions.name: Positive-real frontier compiler handle \(\mathfrak C_p(G,G')\)
definitions.construction: Build the target compiler from terminal-copy min-cut certificates, the sparsely encoded factor-line systems \(\mathfrak B_p(G,G')\), recursive faces of the baseline covariance cone, Schur-complement sign chambers, and branch-gluing certificates; in each semialgebraic chamber \(C\subset\mathcal M_{p,q}(G)\), its output object is either a relatively dense positive-real realization cover or a separator with full dimension relative to \(C\), encoded in the bit model \(\operatorname{Enc}(p,G,G')\).

statements.statement: For every \(\theta\in\mathcal M_{p,q}(G)\), \((I_q-\Lambda^{(k)})^{-1}=P+Pe_kh_k^{\mathsf T}\), \(A^{(k)}=A+a_kh_k^{\mathsf T}\), and \[D_k=a_k(ASh_k)^{\mathsf T}+(ASh_k)a_k^{\mathsf T}+(h_k^{\mathsf T}Sh_k+t_k-v_k)a_ka_k^{\mathsf T}.\] For \(\theta\in\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{branch},p,q}(G,G')\), the systems in \(\mathfrak B_p(G,G')\) represent every legal positive-real covariance twin and no illegal twin, including candidate variance-neutral twins, all loading signs, latent scales, support inequations, and all semialgebraic sign and variance chambers relative to \(\mathcal M_{p,q}(G)\). Exact structural-row change makes the two rank-one directions generically nonproportional at each non-source; at a source, \(h_k=0\), so \(t_k=v_k\) makes the entire intervention null. The factor \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)\) excludes only that nongeneric source-null locus, together with variance-neutral non-source hyperplanes, from the covariance statement. The exceptional product is nonzero on every full-dimensional ambient chamber, and both signs of each true variance change are covered; no pointwise assertion is made on the excluded hyperplanes.
statements.justification: This lemma is the lossless bridge from observed covariance differences to a finite collection of positive candidate mechanisms.
statements.gap: Leyes Carreno et al. give a special overcomplete perfect-intervention covariance nonidentifiability example, not a complete soft-intervention factor-line reduction with positivity.
statements.consumer: This is the exhaustive algebraic input for deciding the covariance side of Problem 5.2 and for the companion LCD workflow's covariance-alternative report.

statements.statement:
For every \(T>0\), \(T
e1\), the two rational parameter points in \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{fork}}(T)\) lie in the semialgebraic ambient domains for \(G_{\mathrm{fork}}\) and \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\), satisfy the required independent centered non-Gaussian distribution conditions, and obey \(\Sigma^{(k)}_{\mathrm{true}}=\Sigma^{(k)}_{\mathrm{candidate}}\) for all five contexts \(k\in K\). The candidate variances \(T+144/121\) and \(19/4\) are positive, all mixing columns are pairwise noncollinear, every changed edge is nonzero and retained, and the corresponding actual-row compatibility obstruction equals \(-2\), so \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}
otin\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G_{\mathrm{fork}})\). No algebraic-independence convention is imposed; membership in a theorem-specific generic locus is determined only by its finite exceptional-polynomial list. The displayed family lies off every true variance-neutral hyperplane because \(T
e1\); the collision and actual-row obstruction do not rely on excluding candidate variance-neutral models.
statements.justification: The explicit rational branch demonstrates that strict positivity is substantive and supplies a checkable worked instance for the compiler.
statements.gap: The anchor contains no positive overcomplete soft-intervention collision with all contexts, support constraints, and actual-row separation checked simultaneously.
statements.consumer: The five covariance identities and the \(-2\) obstruction are a regression fixture for the branch analysis required by Problem 5.2.

statements.statement: For \(p=2\) and \((G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\), the eight loading-line choices are sound and complete on \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{fork},2,4}(G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\), and the finite product defining this locus, including \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)\), is nonzero on every full-dimensional ambient chamber. On each branch, \(v'=v'_0+sn\), \(m_2=\zeta\ell_1+\rho_2\ell_2\), and \(g=v'_1x\ell_1+v'_2\ell_2\); for \(k\in\{3,4\}\), \(\beta_k=\det[m_k,\ell_k]/\det[g,\ell_k]\), \(m_k-\beta_kg=\rho_k\ell_k\), \(h'_k=\beta_k(x,1,0,0)\), and \(t'_k=v'_k+2\rho_k-\beta_k^2(v'_1x^2+v'_2)\), while \(h'_2=(\zeta/v'_1,0,0,0)\) and \(t'_2=v'_2+2\rho_2-\zeta^2/v'_1\). A finite bivariate sign decomposition in \((s,x)\), together with the exact support hyperplane exclusions, classifies the union over every full-dimensional true sign and variance chamber \(C\subset\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{fork},2,4}(G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\) and returns either a legal-twin cover dense relative to \(C\) or a separator with full dimension relative to \(C\), verified in the original five covariance equations. Legal twins may be variance-neutral. In addition, for each \(T>0\), \(T\ne1\), there is a relatively open semialgebraic neighborhood of \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{fork}}(T)\) inside its generic chamber and a legal covariance-twin branch on that neighborhood, certified by a nonzero Jacobian minor from \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{fork}}\). Both signs of every true variance change are covered; no pointwise assertion is made on a true variance-neutral hyperplane.
statements.justification: This is the mandatory first proved deliverable and the early kill test for whether graph-specific branch geometry can replace unrestricted real quantifier elimination.
statements.gap: The closest LCD results give neither an exhaustive positive eight-branch classification nor a nonsingular open covariance collision checked against every original context equation.
statements.consumer: This supplies the smallest auditable instance of the positive-real classification demanded by Problem 5.2 and the template the general compiler must reproduce.

statements.statement: For every \(G'\) with \(\overline{G'}=\overline G\) and every \(\theta\in\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{term},p,q}(G,G')\), \(G'\in\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\) if and only if, for every \(j\in V\), the affine space \(\mathcal A_j\) is nonempty and none of \(x_{ji}\), \(d_{ji}(x_j)\), or \(x_{ji}+d_{ji}(x_j)\), for \(i\in C_j\), vanishes identically on \(\mathcal A_j\). Moreover, \(\operatorname{rank}H[R,C]\) equals the maximum number of vertex-disjoint paths from \(C\) to the terminal copies \(R^{\star}\) in \(G^{\mathrm{term}}\). The finite terminal exceptional product is not identically zero on any full-dimensional ambient chamber, and these conditions yield sound and complete membership and nonmembership certificates in \(O(q^5)\) rational-function field operations. Because this result depends only on structural rows, it holds throughout the positive-variance ambient model, including \(t_k=v_k\).
statements.justification: This is the corrected sound-and-complete combinatorial answer to the compatibility problem before covariance projection.
statements.gap: Definition 3.14 of Leyes Carreno et al. uses observational path ranks and omits the changed-row terminal copies and the finite noncancellation hyperplanes.
statements.consumer: This gives the corrected compatible DAG set and auditable linkage or affine certificates requested by Problem 5.1.

statements.statement: For \(G_{\times}=\{1\to2,2\to3,3\to4,1\to3\}\) and \(G_{\mathrm{ch}}=\{1\to2,2\to3,3\to4\}\), one has \(G_{\mathrm{ch}}\in\mathsf H_{\mathrm{obs}}(G_{\times})\) but \(G_{\mathrm{ch}}\notin\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G_{\times})\) on \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{term},p,4}(G_{\times},G_{\mathrm{ch}})\); the decisive actual-row augmented minor is \(\gamma(\beta d-b\delta)\), which is one explicit member of the finite exceptional-polynomial test and is not the zero polynomial. The mismatch is structural and holds throughout the positive-variance ambient domain.
statements.justification: A generic four-node obstruction establishes that the correction changes the identified graph class rather than only its presentation.
statements.gap: The published substitution treats independent intervention changes as though they were baseline path coefficients; no counterexample is reported there.
statements.consumer: This is a Problem 5.1 regression test preventing the LCD workflow from certifying a chain that violates the actual changed mechanism rows.

statements.statement: For every \(q\)-node DAG \(G\), \[\mathsf H_{\mathrm{obs}}(G)=\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{TRF}(G).\] Equivalently, disagreement occurs exactly when \(G\) contains distinct vertices \(u,k,w\), a directed path of length at least two from \(u\) to \(k\), and edges \(u\to k\) and \(k\to w\). The forbidden configuration is recognizable from the transitive closure in \(O(q^3)\) Boolean operations. Exact enumeration of same-closure candidates and comparison of the two certificate algorithms is only a validation and fixed-instance decision procedure, not the characterization. The equivalence is structural and holds throughout the positive-variance ambient domain.
statements.justification: The forbidden terminal-reuse condition gives an independent graph-theoretic boundary for validity of the published class.
statements.gap: Problem 5.1 asks for a combinatorial description, but the published paper neither audits its observational substitution nor gives a forbidden-configuration characterization of its agreement domain.
statements.consumer: For Problem 5.1, a supplied graph can be screened by transitive closure alone, with enumeration used only to validate an implementation.

statements.statement: For \(p=q\) and every DAG \(G\), \(\mathsf{Cov}_{q}(G)=\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\). For every \(G'\) with \(\overline{G'}=\overline G\), the covariance membership comparison is evaluated on \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{square},q,q}(G,G')\), whose finite exceptional product includes \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)\) and is nonzero in every full-dimensional semialgebraic ambient chamber. The equality is invariant to the common target permutation and covers every loading sign and scale, every exact-support branch, and both signs of every true variance change. Candidate covariance twins range over the full positive-variance ambient class and may be variance-neutral. Exact structural-row change supplies the generic nonproportional-row condition at non-sources, while a source with \(t_k=v_k\) is an entirely null intervention. No pointwise equality is asserted on the true variance-neutral hyperplanes. The retained-edge condition excludes the perfect-intervention regime at every non-source.
statements.justification: Square mixing is the information-frontier benchmark: covariances lose no graph information beyond compatibility of the recovered actual structural rows.
statements.gap: Squires et al. recover the transitive closure from soft-intervention covariances, while Problem 5.2 of Leyes Carreno et al. leaves graph-class equality unresolved.
statements.consumer: For Problem 5.2, the LCD workflow can stop at second moments under square mixing and still report the corrected compatible DAG set.

statements.statement: For every \(2\le p\le q\) and every DAG \(G\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\subseteq\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\) for the generic chamberwise covariance functional. The covariance claim covers both signs of every true variance change and makes no pointwise assertion on the true variance-neutral hyperplanes; candidate twins may be variance-neutral.
statements.justification: The nesting gives the information-order direction needed before equality or strict covariance surplus can be meaningful.
statements.gap: Problem 5.2 states a containment for the published class, but the same relation must be re-established for the corrected actual-row class with candidate mixing admissibility.
statements.consumer: This fixes the information-order direction needed to interpret covariance-only alternatives in Problem 5.2.

statements.statement: If every connected component of \(G\) has at most three vertices, then for every \(2\le p\le q\), \[\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)=\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)=\{G':\overline{G'}=\overline G\}.\] This family contains arbitrarily large DAGs. The covariance equality is generic and chamberwise, covers both signs of every true variance change, allows candidate variance-neutral twins, and makes no pointwise assertion on the true variance-neutral hyperplanes. The retained-edge condition excludes perfect interventions at non-sources.
statements.justification: The proposition supplies the required sanity reduction and an infinite equality family beyond edgeless graphs.
statements.gap: The anchor discusses small examples but does not give an all-\(p\), arbitrarily-large equality family for covariance and actual-row compatibility.
statements.consumer: This gives an infinite family where Problem 5.2 has a complete equality answer without exploring the full branch union.

statements.statement: The recovered relation satisfies \(\mathcal C(\mathcal R)=\overline G\) up to the common latent permutation on \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{term},p,q}(G,G)\cap\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{branch},p,q}(G,G)\). The maps \(\mathcal R\mapsto\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R)\) and \((\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K})\mapsto\mathcal G_{\mathrm{cov}}(\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K})\) are invariant to the choice of representative of \(\mathcal R\) under \(\mathfrak M_q\). If the inputs arise from \(\theta\in\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{term},p,q}(G,G)\cap\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{branch},p,q}(G,G)\cap\mathcal M^{\circ}_{s,p,q}(G,G')\) for the relevant covariance theorem label \(s\), then \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R)=\{\Pi_M(G'):G'\in\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G),\ M\in\mathfrak M_q\}\) and \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{cov}}(\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K})=\{\Pi_M(G'):G'\in\mathsf{Cov}_{p}(G),\ M\in\mathfrak M_q\}\), where \(\Pi_M\) is the permutation part of \(M\). Hence the target is a functional of the explicit aligned factor input and covariance tuple, not a functional indexed by an unobserved true graph. This generic observable statement makes no pointwise assertion when a true variance change vanishes.
statements.justification: This proposition makes the population target invariant to the unavoidable latent permutation and scaling ambiguity.
statements.gap: The comparator results recover latent factors or graph classes only up to relabeling; they do not state this corrected covariance-versus-actual-row pair as one quotient-valued data functional.
statements.consumer: This supplies Problems 5.1--5.2 with a graph-class target defined from aligned population factors and covariances rather than the unobserved true graph.

statements.statement: Construct \(\mathfrak C_p(G,G')\) so that, for every \(2\le p<q\) and every same-transitive-closure pair \((G,G')\), it decides whether \(G'\in\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\setminus\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\). Prove soundness and completeness over the union of all legal positive-real branches in every full-dimensional semialgebraic sign and variance chamber \(C\subset\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{branch},p,q}(G,G')\), with every closure and relative-interior claim taken in \(C\), and prove termination without invoking unrestricted real quantifier elimination. Candidate twins range over the full positive-variance ambient class and may be variance-neutral. Generic reasoning may discard only the zero set of the finite family \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{branch}}(p,G,G')\), including \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)\), whose product must be proved nonzero on each relevant chamber. In the encoding \(\operatorname{Enc}(p,G,G')\), give a closed-form bit-operation bound as a function of \(p\), \(q\), \(B\), and the branch count \(2^{q-r}\), including coefficient growth; a field-operation count alone does not qualify. On acceptance return a chamberwise dense positive-real realization cover, and on rejection return a checkable full-dimensional linkage, affine, covariance-cone-face, or positivity separator. Use the compiler to produce infinite equality families and infinite families with generic strict covariance surplus. Cover both signs of every true variance change, but make no pointwise assertion on true variance-neutral hyperplanes.
statements.justification: The compiler is the theorem-level kernel that turns Problem 5.2 for the covariance and aligned-factor compatibility classes into a graph-specific positive-real information frontier.
statements.gap: Leyes Carreno et al. pose covariance strictness but do not retain all real positivity branches; Kela et al. cover a convex bipartite cone, and Boege--Solus require a birational map rather than an overcomplete branch union.
statements.consumer: This would answer Problem 5.2 graph by graph and let the companion LCD workflow attach either a covariance realization or a separator certificate.

sampling_model.design: Population identification from one baseline context and one unknown-target single-node soft-intervention context per latent node, restricted in this paper to square or overcomplete latent mixing \(2\le p\le q\). Baseline and intervened structural error variances are positive and may coincide.
sampling_model.units: The inputs are the aligned population factorization datum \(\mathcal R\) and the \(q+1\) population covariance matrices \(\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K}\); no finite-sample asymptotic claim is made.
sampling_model.treatment: Intervention targets are unknown and are identified only up to one common latent-node permutation. Every non-source intervention changes and retains each incoming edge. At a source, \(t_k=v_k\) makes the intervention null because there is no structural row to change.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition applies. Positivity, closure, relative interior, and chamber statements are relative to the semialgebraic ambient coefficient domain \(\mathcal M_{p,q}(G)\). Covariance frontier theorems work on theorem-specific generic loci that exclude \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)=0\), cover both adjacent sign chambers, and make no pointwise assertion on those hyperplanes.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The aligned factor matrices and source laws modulo one common permutation and diagonal scaling are explicit population inputs. Recovery from raw laws and noisy tensor estimation are outside the theorem scope.

estimand_functional: \((\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K})\longmapsto(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R),\mathcal G_{\mathrm{cov}}(\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K}))\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Definition 3.14 and Theorem 1.7 identify the soft-compatible DAG class by generic ranks of baseline inverse-path submatrices.
Under Assumption 1, Theorem 1 recovers only the transitive closure from generic soft interventions; its second clause recovers the full DAG under Assumption 2 perfect interventions.
Theorem 2.8 characterizes generic covariance-submatrix rank by trek separation.
The half-trek criterion gives a polynomial-time sufficient certificate for generic rational identifiability.
Theorem 1 gives recursive rational recovery from latent-factor half-trek systems, with efficient bounded search.
Supported positive-semidefinite covariance decompositions are necessary and realizable for bipartite latent causal structures.
Theorem 3.15 of arXiv version 1 gives positive-denominator birational implicitization of a semialgebraic model image.

tldr: Soft-intervention LCD compatibility must be defined by the actual changed mechanism rows \(h_k^{\mathsf T}=\delta_k^{\mathsf T}(I_q-\Lambda^{(0)})^{-1}\), not by observational path rows. The paper deliberately restricts attention to square mixing \(p=q\), where the generic covariance class equals the corrected actual-row class, and overcomplete latent mixing \(p<q\), where covariance projection is genuinely noninjective; this restriction is not part of the cited standard LCD regime. The positive-support semialgebraic ambient model allows \(t_k=v_k\). Only the theorem-specific covariance loci include \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)\) in their finite exceptional products, cover both adjacent sign chambers, and make no pointwise assertion on the neutral hyperplanes; terminal compatibility itself has no variance-activity restriction. Conditional on aligned population factors modulo common permutation and scaling, the observable target is the pair of factor-compatible and covariance-compatible DAG sets on the recovered transitive closure. The mandatory first deliverable classifies all eight bivariate branches of the \(p=2,q=4\) fork and certifies a nonsingular open collision before the graph-specific non-quantifier-elimination compiler is attempted.

project_justification.gap: Problem 5.1 asks for a combinatorial description of the published soft-compatible class and Problem 5.2 asks whether the covariance-compatible and factor-compatible DAG classes differ. The proof behind Definition 3.14 replaces intervention-change path sums by observational path sums, and the inspected literature has no all-branch positive-real covariance criterion for overcomplete soft LCD. A generic formulation based on algebraic independence would also fail to specify the positive-real ambient topology or the finite exceptional sets used by each theorem.
project_justification.niche: Actual intervention rows create a terminal-copy path matroid coupled to affine noncancellation. Within the paper-specific range \(p\le q\), the square case is an injective information benchmark, while the overcomplete latent case creates a finite union of factor-line projections with strict positivity. The ambient model contains all positive structural error variances, including neutral hyperplanes. Covariance theorems use explicit finite exceptional products and full-dimensional sign chambers, whereas the terminal theory does not require variance activity.
project_justification.fill: The terminal certificate corrects the factor-compatible graph class, and the forbidden terminal-reuse theorem characterizes exactly when the published class survives throughout the positive-variance ambient domain. Square whitening closes the generic injective frontier, subject to proof. The explicit eight-branch fork classification is the first deliverable, and the positive-real compiler targets the remaining overcomplete frontier with realizations, separators, termination, and bit complexity. The data functional is defined only from aligned population factors and covariances modulo the common latent ambiguity.

related_work: Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025) provide the ambient LCD setup, Theorem 1.7, Definition 3.14, and Problems 5.1--5.2; the restriction \(p\le q\) is maintained by this paper rather than attributed to that setup, and the actual-row result strictly tightens their compatibility characterization throughout the positive-variance ambient domain. Squires, Seigal, Bhate, and Uhler (2023) inform the square argument through rank-two covariance differences, ancestor-order recovery, partial-order RQ factorization, and Cholesky reconstruction: under their Assumption 1, generic soft interventions recover only the transitive closure, while the second clause of their Theorem 1 recovers the full DAG under Assumption 2 perfect interventions. The retained-edge condition here excludes perfect interventions at every non-source, so the square equality is not a restatement of that full-DAG clause. Zhang et al. (2023) obtain an injective soft-intervention equivalence class under linear interventional and adjacency faithfulness, which does not characterize the overcomplete covariance fiber considered here. Sullivant, Talaska, and Draisma (2010) and Foygel, Draisma, and Drton (2012) inform the terminal-copy determinant cancellation and max-flow certificate. Foygel Barber et al. (2022) show how graph-explicit latent-factor linkages can support rational recovery, but their criterion concerns one covariance model rather than a shared-context positive projection. Kela et al. (2020) inform the realization-or-separator format for positive-semidefinite covariance compatibility; their feasible cone is convex and bipartite. Theorem 3.15 of Boege and Solus (2024), arXiv version 1, informs exact positive-denominator birational implicitization; its birational hypothesis does not settle the overcomplete union of branches. Variance-neutral points belong to this paper's ambient model; only generic covariance conclusions exclude the true neutral hyperplanes through explicit theorem-specific exceptional products.
technical_internal_limitation: Exact symbolic evidence establishes a four-node observational-substitution obstruction, positive square examples, a lossless regular reduction of one \(p=2\) fork pair to eight bivariate systems, and a rational covariance collision with positive candidate variances \(T+144/121\) and \(19/4\) for every \(T>0\), \(T\ne1\). Finite enumeration validates small instances but does not prove the terminal-reuse-free if-and-only-if characterization. The eight-branch theorem must still prove its full chamber classification and nonsingular open continuation inside the covariance-generic locus; isolated rational points do not do so. The finite branch, square, and fork exceptional products include \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)\), so the covariance results make no pointwise assertion on those hyperplanes. Exact structural-row change already supplies the generic nonproportional-row condition at non-sources; only a source with \(t_k=v_k\) is entirely null. A nonsingular local branch, complex dominance, or unrestricted real quantifier elimination does not supply the general compiler.
honest_scope: The scope \(2\le p\le q\) is deliberate: \(p=q\) supplies the square benchmark and \(p<q\) is the overcomplete latent frontier; no claim is made for \(p>q\). The positive-support ambient model retains every \(v_k>0\) and \(t_k>0\), including \(t_k=v_k\). Terminal-copy compatibility, the forbidden terminal-reuse characterization, and the published-class mismatch are structural claims across that ambient domain. Covariance branch, fork, square, nesting, small-component, and compiler claims are generic and chamberwise: their finite exceptional products include \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)\), they cover both signs of every true variance change, and they make no pointwise assertion on the neutral hyperplanes. Candidate covariance twins remain in the full positive-variance ambient class and may be neutral. At a non-source, exact nonzero structural-row change supplies the generic nonproportional-row condition; at a source, \(t_k=v_k\) yields an entirely null intervention and is excluded only from covariance theorem loci. The retained-edge condition rules out perfect interventions at every non-source. The mandatory first proved deliverable is the full eight-branch \(p=2,q=4\) fork classification, including an original-equation certificate and a nonsingular open collision. The terminal-copy certificate, forbidden terminal-reuse characterization, covariance branch reduction, square equality, and small-component equality family remain statements to prove. The genuinely open kernel is the uniform graph-specific compiler for \(p<q\). The estimand is conditional on aligned population factors modulo common permutation and scaling; recovery from raw laws, finite-sample confidence sets, missing interventions, multitarget interventions, and nonlinear mixing are outside scope. As a sanity reduction, the corrected and covariance classes both collapse generically to the full same-transitive-closure class on components of size at most three, and square mixing gives \(\mathsf{Cov}_q(G)=\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\), both subject to proof.

seed_details.opportunity: For \(p<q\), characterize exactly when every legal positive-real covariance branch projects densely relative to each full-dimensional chamber of the semialgebraic ambient domain and when a relatively open covariance-only graph alternative remains in such a chamber.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the anchor's dimension count for one perfect-intervention fiber by the exact rank-two covariance-difference factorization, then retain shared mixing, exact support, and Schur-complement positivity across all contexts.
seed_details.destination_search: Bounded exact-title and target--method searches for overcomplete soft-intervention covariance compatibility, positive-real projection completeness, and graph-specific non-quantifier-elimination criteria found no result occupying this target.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may call the result immediate from real quantifier elimination because every branch is semialgebraic.
seed_details.rebuttal: The deliverable forbids unrestricted elimination and requires a graph-specific realization-or-separator invariant with an explicit complexity bound; neither the anchor nor general semialgebraic decidability supplies that structure.

seed_details.opportunity: Replace observational-path ranks by the actual changed mechanism rows, give an if-and-only-if terminal-copy strict-gammoid plus affine-hyperplane certificate, and characterize agreement with the published class by absence of a transitive edge entering a nonsink.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Do not replace \((\Lambda^{(k)}-\Lambda^{(0)})\)-weighted path sums by baseline edge weights; expand minors in a graph with independent terminal copies instead.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining soft compatibility, actual intervention rows, terminal copies, and affine-span certificates found the anchor but no correction or complete graph algorithm.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may say genericity in Theorem 3.15 already licenses the substitution.
seed_details.rebuttal: The determinant \(\gamma(\beta d-b\delta)\) is a nonzero member of the finite terminal exceptional-polynomial family when the observational-path determinant is identically zero, so independent changed-row coefficients invalidate that substitution on the stated relative Zariski-open locus.

seed_details.opportunity: Prove \(\mathsf{Cov}_{q}(G)=\mathsf{H}_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\) for square mixing, uniformly over target permutations, loading signs and scales, exact supports, and positive variance chambers relative to \(\mathcal M_{q,q}(G)\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Upgrade the anchor's unconstrained covariance fiber comparison to baseline whitening and inductive elimination of the alternate loading line using the recovered ancestor order.
seed_details.destination_search: The closest destination paper, SquiresSeigalBhateUhler2023, recovers the transitive closure from soft-intervention covariances under injective mixing but does not compare covariance compatibility with corrected actual-row compatibility.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may regard this as a restatement of injective covariance recovery in Squires et al.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their soft-intervention result identifies only the transitive closure, whereas equality here must characterize every same-closure graph surviving all positive candidate branches and must incorporate the corrected actual rows.

seed_details.opportunity: Construct a finite birational atlas for regular covariance branches that transports every variance inequality and support inequation to observed covariance coordinates.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Boege and Solus start from a globally rationally identifiable parametrization; overcomplete LCD instead requires branchwise rational inverse charts and a proof that their positive images cover the generic fiber.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for ambirational soft-intervention LCD and branchwise positive covariance charts found no application to shared overcomplete mixing.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may say this is a direct application of real birational implicitization.
seed_details.rebuttal: The LCD map is not globally birational when \(p<q\); the missing theorem is precisely finite chart coverage and gluing across nonunique positive decompositions.

seed_details.opportunity: Derive a hierarchy of covariance-cone face separators that is complete for selected soft-intervention graph families and returns a positive realization on acceptance.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace independent positive-semidefinite components supported by a bipartite graph with context-coupled rank-one differences sharing one mixing matrix and one structural inverse.
seed_details.destination_search: The searched covariance-compatibility literature provides convex primal and dual certificates for bipartite latent structures, not a complete separator hierarchy for the nonconvex shared-context LCD image.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may say semidefinite duality already gives every required separator.
seed_details.rebuttal: The graph-realization equations make the LCD feasible set a finite union of nonconvex projections, so the Kela et al. cone is only an outer relaxation unless branch coupling is proved complete.

seed_details.opportunity: Prove that the published observational-path class agrees with actual-row compatibility exactly for terminal-reuse-free DAGs, equivalently those with no transitive edge entering a nonsink.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Compare original-terminal and copied-terminal path matroids before solving the affine child-column systems.
seed_details.destination_search: No forbidden-subgraph or matroid-minor characterization of this published class was located; the available anchor gives only rank tests.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may say enumeration of all same-closure DAGs is already an exact characterization.
seed_details.rebuttal: Enumeration is retained only as a validation oracle; the theorem-level target is the forbidden terminal-reuse equivalence, recognizable directly from the transitive closure.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace latent-factor half-trek recovery of one coefficient column by dynamic programming over covariance factor-line branches and terminal-copy separators.
seed_details.destination_search: The latent-factor half-trek paper proves polynomial checking only when searched latent sets are bounded and shows unrestricted checking is hard; no corresponding soft-LCD covariance-frontier algorithm was found.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may call bounded width an arbitrary tractable subclass.
seed_details.rebuttal: It is defensible only if the width is the maximum terminal separator governing actual-row rank and yields a sharp complexity transition; otherwise this seed is dropped.

seed_details.destination_search: No finite-sample test was found for the corrected soft-LCD compatibility class; existing covariance witness proposals do not estimate overcomplete intervention factor lines.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may say sample splitting after a population certificate is routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: The statistical problem is not credible until the population branch-union separator exists and its estimation stability is quantified, so this is deferred rather than padded into the core.
